title: Kingdom of Galicia
capsule: The Kingdom of Galicia in northwestern Iberia emerged as an independent polity when the Suevic kingdom was absorbed and the territory later passed under Visigothic control before re-emerging under Ordoño I and Alfonso III as part of the Asturian-Leonese reconquest framework. It was periodically ruled as a separate kingdom and at times a co-kingdom with León, with Sancho II and Alfonso VI contesting its control in the 1060s–70s; Alfonso VI made his brother García king of Galicia in 1065. The kingdom lost independent status when it was definitively subsumed within the Kingdom of León in 1126 under Alfonso VII, though it retained its name as a distinct realm within Iberian royal titulature.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's outer borders are broadly attested in chronicles, but precise boundaries at any given decade are poorly recorded; internal political status (independent vs. sub-kingdom of León) shifted repeatedly.
